# i18n.hreflang — hreflang alternate set is not reciprocal or points at a page that does not exist

- **Check ID:** `i18n.hreflang`
- **Default severity:** `warning`; users can override it in `seaworthy.config.json`.
- **Needs:** `html`
- **Standards:** Google rel=alternate hreflang
- **Source module:** `packages/verify/src/checks/i18n.ts`
- **Prose page:** [`docs/checks/i18n.hreflang.md`](../i18n.hreflang.md) — embedded below verbatim; write it there, never here.

A `rel="alternate" hreflang=...` link set is not reciprocal, or one of its entries points at a page the built site does not serve.

## Why it matters

`hreflang` alternates tell search engines and agents which page serves which language. The contract is mutual: when page A declares that page U serves language X, page U must declare a link back to A for A's language, and both must exist in the build. One dangling URL or one missing back-link makes engines distrust the whole set, and agents that follow the undeclared path land on the wrong language or an error page.

## What it checks

For every page, each `<link rel="alternate" hreflang="X" href="U">` (HTTP `Link` headers are not read) must satisfy two rules:

- **Existence:** U resolves to a page of the built site the way a static host serves it (`/dir/` to its `index.html`, extensionless URLs, the configured `basePath`). Only entries inside this build are checked: an `hreflang` pointing at another site is skipped without a report and never fetched, so the check stays offline.
- **Reciprocity:** the page that U serves must declare an alternate whose `hreflang` equals the declaring page's own language key (from `<html lang>`, compared without regard to case, so `EN` and `en` are the same language) and whose `href` points back at the declaring page.

`x-default` entries are not a language and are left out of scope here; a follow-up check (`i18n.x-default`) covers them. A page with no `<html lang>` declares no language key, so nothing can be demanded back from its targets and it degrades to silence. A page holding only self-referencing entries for its own language is correct.

## How to fix

```html
<!-- before: /de/about.html declares no alternate back to /about.html -->
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="de" href="/de/about.html">
<!-- after: declare both directions, including each page's self-reference -->
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="de" href="/de/about.html">
<!-- and in /de/about.html -->
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="/about.html">
```

The report points at the `hreflang` attribute that starts the broken direction and gives the exact link to add to the other page. Remove alternates for pages that are not translations of each other. **Fix it in the source** (templates or the i18n plugin that emits the tags), not in the built file.

## Options

None.

## Standards

- [Google: Tell Google about localized versions of your page](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/localized-versions)
